result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street with sidewalks on both sides, though the right side is bordered by a long fence and blank frontage. The environment lacks formal pedestrian crossings and traffic calming measures, and the roadway pavement is in poor condition.

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The roadway surface is heavily cracked and degraded, which can cause tripping hazards or lead to unpredictable vehicle movements.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A chair and other debris are located on the left sidewalk, narrowing the usable walking path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left sidewalk near the white house

hazards.name: Lack of Passive Surveillance
hazards.description: The right side of the street is a long, opaque fence/wall, creating a 'dead' streetscape that can feel unsafe for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Roadway and Sidewalk Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and repave the street and sidewalks to eliminate trip hazards and improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at the end of the block to provide a designated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Streetscape Improvements
interventions.description: Introduce street trees or lighting along the right-hand fence line to improve the pedestrian experience and perceived safety.

result.summary: The image shows a wide concrete sidewalk adjacent to a multi-story brick residential building. A large mature tree is situated within the sidewalk area, and the pavement shows signs of wear with cracks and emerging vegetation.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: Cracks and weeds at the base of the tree and across the sidewalk panels create potential trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground sidewalk area around the tree base

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer or furniture zone separating the walking path from the adjacent roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Edge of the sidewalk adjacent to the curb

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Maintenance
interventions.description: Repair cracked concrete panels and clear weeds to ensure a smooth, accessible walking surface.

interventions.title: Tree Pit Improvement
interventions.description: Install a formal tree grate or expanded planting bed to protect the tree roots and level the walking surface.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features continuous sidewalks and a stop-controlled intersection, but safety is compromised by vehicles parked on the walkway and poor sightlines. While basic crosswalk markings are present, the lack of high-visibility infrastructure and the presence of sidewalk obstructions increase risk for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A silver van is parked directly on the sidewalk on the right side of the street, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction at Intersection
hazards.description: The parked van near the corner obscures sightlines between pedestrians waiting to cross and approaching vehicles.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The existing parallel-line crosswalk markings are standard and appear somewhat worn, reducing their visibility to drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near the intersection and install physical barriers like bollards to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade the intersection with continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and prevent illegal parking on the sidewalk or near corners.

result.summary: The image depicts a standard urban residential environment with a continuous, paved sidewalk adjacent to a brick building. While the walkway is clear and in good condition, there is no physical buffer between pedestrians and the roadway other than a lane of parallel-parked cars.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars obscures the sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lane, increasing risk for mid-block crossings.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and right side of the image along the curb.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Incorporate a dedicated furniture or planting zone between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical buffer from traffic and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to ensure the walkway and any potential crossing points are well-illuminated at night.
